findings.title: Create agent endpoint changes status code from 201 to 200
findings.rationale: The handler for POST /agents now returns HTTP 200 instead of 201. Any deployed caller (web client, e2e tests, CI runner, external consumer) that expects a 201 status on successful agent creation will break silently or fail assertions. The 201 status is the standard for resource creation and is widely relied upon. The compatible alternative is to keep 201 for this endpoint, or to introduce a new route that returns 200 while preserving the old one for one release cycle.

findings.title: Client calls non-existent server endpoint
findings.rationale: The new `downloadFindingsCsv` function fetches from `/pulls/${prId}/findings.csv`. No server route for this path is added in this PR. Any caller (the web client) that triggers this export will receive a 404 response and throw an error. The feature is broken until the server-side implementation is included.

findings.title: CSV export fetch omits authentication headers
findings.rationale: The function uses a bare `fetch` without any credentials or authorization headers. The existing `apiFetch` (used by all other API calls) likely attaches an auth token (e.g., Bearer token from session). If the new endpoint requires authentication, this call will fail with 401/403. The PR description states this is intentional because the response is a blob, but the auth mechanism should still be applied.

findings.title: New function not integrated into `api` object
findings.rationale: All other API calls are methods on the `api` object (e.g., `api.get`, `api.post`). Adding `downloadFindingsCsv` as a standalone export breaks the pattern and may confuse future maintainers. While not a contract issue, consistency improves readability.

findings.title: CSV export fetch may not send authentication cookies in cross-origin setups
findings.rationale: The new `downloadFindingsCsv` function uses a plain `fetch` call without specifying `credentials`. The existing `apiFetch` (used by all other API calls) likely includes credentials (e.g., `credentials: 'include'`). If `API_BASE` is a different origin (common in development with separate ports), the CSV request will not send cookies, causing a 401/403 response. This breaks the new feature for any deployment where the API is not same-origin. The fix is to add `credentials: 'include'` (or `'same-origin'` if appropriate) to the fetch options.

Compatible alternative: use the existing `apiFetch` with `responseType: 'blob'` or add `credentials: 'include'` and pass the auth token from the API context.

findings.title: Unhandled promise rejection in button onClick handler
findings.rationale: The async onClick function throws an error if the fetch fails, but there is no `.catch()` or try/catch. This will result in an unhandled promise rejection and no user feedback. While the UI still works for successful requests, failures are silent and may confuse users.
